title: Two British Men Indicted in Iran-Linked Terror Plot Targeting U.S. Air Base in UK
snippet: British prosecutors have charged two men in connection with a suspected Iranian-backed plot targeting RAF Fairford, a strategic air base used by U.S. bombers.
content:
LONDON — British counter-terrorism authorities have charged two London residents in connection with a suspected state-sponsored plot targeting RAF Fairford, a key military installation in western England heavily utilized by the U.S. Air Force.

Mohmed Ahmad Abdulkarim and Nouman Essghir, both 24-year-old British citizens, face serious national security offenses. Crown prosecutors stated that Abdulkarim is accused of assisting Iran’s intelligence apparatus, while Essghir has been charged with entering a prohibited site for purposes hostile to U.K. interests.

A Hostile Operation Targeting American Military Assets

RAF Fairford serves as a crucial forward-operating hub for American heavy bombers, which have recently launched missions against targets in Iran. The security breach prompted the U.S. military to temporarily withdraw its aircraft from the installation as a protective measure.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham indicated that the covert plot was "almost certainly" orchestrated by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). While Iranian officials denied involvement, Tehran has previously asserted that any foreign facility supporting military action against its homeland constitutes a valid target.

Evacuations and Explosive Sweeps

The investigation unfolded dramatically on September 27 when armed counter-terrorism officers and military bomb-disposal units converged outside the air base, arresting Essghir. Authorities ordered immediate evacuations of neighboring residential areas while sweeps were conducted. While bomb technicians found no active explosive devices, investigators uncovered significant quantities of gasoline inside vans parked near the facility.

Essghir was initially released on bail before being taken back into custody last week alongside Abdulkarim. Six additional suspects remain on bail as counter-terrorism detectives continue their inquiry.

Escalating European Threat Environment

The charges arrive amid stark warnings from senior Western intelligence officials regarding aggressive espionage and sabotage campaigns orchestrated by hostile foreign states.

Ken McCallum, head of the U.K.’s domestic intelligence service MI5, recently warned that state-backed threats from both Iran and Russia are surging across Britain. McCallum noted that British authorities have disrupted dozens of Iran-linked plots in the past year alone, emphasizing that Tehran is expanding its target list beyond Iranian dissidents to include critical infrastructure and strategic military targets.
